summary: This informational memo recommends reclassifying RFC 1888, which dealt with OSI NSAPs and IPv6, as Historic. It says most of that document has no further value, and that one section is faulty.

eli5.summary: This document says an older rulebook is out of date and should be put on the shelf, because most of it is no longer useful and one part is wrong.

subtitle: A short memo recommending that RFC 1888, on OSI addresses inside IPv6, be reclassified as Historic.

tldr.problem: RFC 1888 defined mappings between OSI NSAP addresses and IPv6 addresses, but one set of mappings was never used and the other had errors.
tldr.mechanism: This memo explains the lack of use and the two errors in the IDP format description, and recommends that the IESG reclassify RFC 1888 as Historic.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1888 is obsolete. Anyone who wants the IPv6-in-NSAP mapping is expected to correct it and resubmit it as a separate document.

today: RFC 4048 is Informational and obsoletes RFC 1888. It has since been updated by RFC 4548.

sections.title: What RFC 1888 Defined
sections.content:
RFC 1888 was published as an Experimental RFC in 1996, early in IPv6 development, when it seemed important to consider using Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) addressing for IPv6. In its Sections 3 through 5 it maps certain OSI NSAP addresses inside IPv6 addresses and shows how to carry arbitrary NSAP addresses as IPv6 destination options.

It also carried significant "health warnings" about how hard it is to route packets in the global Internet using such addresses. As far as the IETF knew, these mappings had never been seriously used and were not supported by IPv6 implementations, and OSI deployment was not widespread enough to change that.
sections.eli5: The old book showed how to hide one kind of address inside another. It warned that this would be hard to use, and nobody ever really did it.

sections.title: Two Errors in Section 6
sections.content:
Section 6 of RFC 1888 goes the other way and maps IPv6 addresses inside OSI NSAP addresses. This had recently attracted some interest, for example to express IP addresses in an Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) context.

The memo says this section misuses the OSI Initial Domain Part (IDP) format in two ways:

  • It treats the Internet Code Point (ICP) as a single octet, when it is correctly a 16-bit field.
  • It says the first three octets are an IDP in binary format, but the OSI network service definition says the abstract syntax for the IDI is decimal digits, with a preferred binary encoding that uses a semi-octet for each digit (values 0000-1001).
sections.eli5: The other half of the book was useful to some people, but it had two mistakes in how it wrote down the address labels.

sections.title: Recommendation and IANA Actions
sections.content:
Because one mapping was unused and the other was documented incorrectly, the memo recommends that the IESG reclassify RFC 1888 as Historic. It assumes that parties who want to map IPv6 addresses inside OSI NSAP addresses will correct, augment and resubmit Section 6 as a separate document.

IANA has marked the IPv6 address prefix 0000 001, which RFC 3513 reserved for NSAP allocation, simply as Reserved. The registry for the "OSI NSAPA Internet Code Point" implied by Section 6 is held in abeyance until a replacement for that section is approved. The memo sees no known impact on Internet security.
sections.eli5: The note says to retire the book. If someone still wants the useful half, they should fix it and write it up again as a new note.

references.text: Bound, J., Carpenter, B., Harrington, D., Houldsworth, J., and A. Lloyd, "OSI NSAPs and IPv6", RFC 1888, August 1996.
